title: Bounded encoded simulation configurations are admissible
statement: Let $R$ be a natural number, let $P$ be a counter program with $R$ registers and label set $\Lambda$, and fix an initial label $l_0$, a Boolean flag $\ell$, natural numbers $n,p,B$, a bit string $u$, and a function $o:\{0,1\}\to\{0,1\}^*$. Suppose that for every natural number $h$, $o(0,\langle 1^n,\mathrm{bits}(h)\rangle)$ is true exactly when $h<|u|$, and $o(1,\langle 1^n,\mathrm{bits}(h)\rangle)$ equals the $h$-th bit of $u$, with false returned when that bit is out of range. For any label $q$ and register assignment $\rho$ with $\rho(r)\le B$ for every register $r$, and any $p_*,o_*,t_*\le B$, the configuration with label $q$, register values obtained by extending $\rho$ with the values $p_*,o_*,t_*$, and no output bit satisfies the simulation invariant at input $\langle 1^n,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle$ and bound $B$.
hypotheses_covered: The output oracle $o$ returns the length test on encoded indices for every $h$
The output oracle $o$ returns the corresponding bit of $u$, defaulting to false out of range, for every $h$
Every register value of $\rho$ is at most $B$
caveat: The conclusion uses a simulation invariant whose admissibility condition depends on the program instruction at the configuration label; the formal statement supplies that condition through definitions not informally described in the payload.
